question.text: A particle travels along a straight path with a velocity that varies with time as depicted in the graph. Draw the corresponding position-time (s−t) graph of the motion, given that the particle is at s = 0 when t = 0.
conditions: velocity increases linearly from 0 to 10 m/s between t = 0 and t = 2 s
velocity remains constant at 10 m/s between t = 2 s and t = 4 s
velocity increases linearly from 10 m/s to 20 m/s between t = 4 s and t = 6 s
velocity decreases linearly from 20 m/s to 0 m/s between t = 6 s and t = 8 s

figure.description: A velocity-time (v−t) graph with v (in m/s) on the vertical axis and t (in s) on the horizontal axis. The graph consists of four straight-line segments connecting the points: O(0, 0) to A(2, 10), A(2, 10) to B(4, 10), B(4, 10) to C(6, 20), and C(6, 20) to D(8, 0).

solution.approach: Find the displacement at each corner time from the area under the v-t graph, then describe the curvature of the s-t graph in each interval.

steps.text: Find the displacement at t = 2, 4, 6, 8 s by adding the area under each straight segment of the v-t graph.
From 0 to 2 s the velocity rises from 0 to 10 m/s, so the s-t curve is concave up, steepening. From 2 to 4 s the velocity is constant at 10 m/s, so the s-t curve is a straight line.
steps.equation: 0–2 s: concave up, 2–4 s: straight line of slope 10

steps.text: From 4 to 6 s the velocity rises again from 10 to 20 m/s, so the s-t curve is concave up, steepening further. From 6 to 8 s the velocity falls from 20 to 0, so the s-t curve is concave down, flattening to a horizontal tangent at t = 8 s.
steps.equation: 4–6 s: concave up, 6–8 s: concave down, tangent horizontal at t = 8 s

final_answer.value: The s-t graph passes through (0,0), (2,10), (4,30), (6,60), (8,80) m in metres and seconds. It is concave up on 0–2 s and 4–6 s, a straight line on 2–4 s, and concave down on 6–8 s, flattening to a horizontal tangent at the maximum displacement of 80 m at t = 8 s.

common_mistakes.text: Drawing straight lines between the four displacement values ignores that the velocity is changing within each interval, which curves the s-t graph rather than making it a series of straight segments.
